phase: Paused for the night — resume from docs/port/RESUME.md
summary: Porting the FFT ocean from WebGL2 / three 0.180 to WebGPU / TSL on three r186 as the @dreamp/world-ocean engine module. Low tier first, then medium, high and ultra; each piece is built, then reviewed against the WebGL reference by a separate critic until it passes.

shots.label: Milestone: first WebGPU FFT ocean (C1 storm camera, interim material, no foam history yet)
shots.caption: GPU FFT fields match the CPU core to 4e-7 of Hs on every tier

pieces.name: Infra: package scaffold, contract stubs, demo shell, capture harness, reference captures
pieces.verdict: Headless Edge gets the RTX 2070 WebGPU adapter; 27 reference shots captured; demo shell renders via WebGPU

pieces.name: Core: JONSWAP spectrum, CPU FFT, WATER_QUERY, presets, Node tests
pieces.verdict: Review r2 FAIL (docs/port/reviews/core-r2.md): tick itself 0.2 ms, but tick + gameplay queries p99 6.8–8.7 ms (11–15 ms without workers); two worker blockers (late job corrupts heights up to 7 m; crash hangs main thread); workers never run in the browser; time clamp breaks height-at-time; heightAt 0.5 M/s. Round 2: snapshot workers + lazy velocity: first velocityAt 6.1 → 0.1 ms, paced tick+queries p99 3.1 ms (idle machine), 0 B per tick, presets renamed (calm 0.54 / breeze 1.46 / windy 4.04 = reference / storm 9.0 m Hs); heightAt 0.4–0.6 M/s with cubic filter. Under review. Round 1 FAIL: fidelity and determinism verified, but tick + gameplay queries average 10.4 ms (p99 20 ms) because velocityAt fills whole frames; small per-tick allocations. Builder sent back.

pieces.name: Reference analysis of the WebGL ocean (feature checklist)
pieces.verdict: 27-item visual checklist F1–F27, 7 canonical cameras; reference Hs 2.18 / 2.58 / 4.07 m

pieces.name: GPU FFT in TSL compute, all four tiers
pieces.verdict: Round 3: same sea on every tier (paused tier switch leaves large waves pixel-identical); every tier < 2 % Hs vs the CPU query; low 0.12 ms / 8.8 MB, medium 0.16 ms / 12.9 MB. Review once the core's cubic query lands. Round 2: cost scaled (low 3.2 MB / 0.06 ms, medium 12.8 MB / 0.16 ms), non-blocking tier switch, Catmull-Rom near camera. Rejected by orchestrator: per-tier band re-cut changes the sea itself between tiers; round 3 enforces tier invariance. Round 1 FAIL: wave-for-wave match with the reference verified, but tiers didn't scale cost (low ≈ medium, ultra zero-padded), bilinear instead of bicubic displacement, ultra switch blocks 55–76 ms. Builder sent back.

pieces.name: Camera-relative LOD mesh + floating origin
pieces.verdict: Round 3: separate far-plane horizon closure (0/36 hidden-island cases), double-buffered tier swap (ultra swap frame 14.5 → 2.2 ms), float64 camera-relative clipPosition (bit-identical at 1e5/1e7), sector frustum culling (drawn triangles 602k → 239k). Needs index.ts wiring (routed to the material builder); not yet re-reviewed. Round 2 FAIL (close): no gaps anywhere, but the skirt wins depth ties and hides terrain beyond ~0.985 far; tier swap upload hitch 14.5 ms on ultra; mediump model-view shifts the sea 0.5 m at 1e7 m. Round 3 building. Earlier: horizon closed at far 3000/5000/20000/∞ (288 shots, 0 gaps), sliced non-blocking tier build, ?origin fixed, motion vectors for morph/skirt; under review. Round 1 FAIL: watertight and origin-exact, but the horizon skirt depends on camera.far (gap at far=5000, vanishes at far=Infinity); tier change stalls 21–68 ms. Builder sent back.

pieces.name: Water material: reflection, sun, body colour, SSS
pieces.verdict: Round 2: shaded image bit-identical at origin 1e5/1e7 (view vector from view space); foam/rim lit from SKY_LIGHT (dark at night); no double sun dimming; motion vectors wired into three's velocity pipeline via setMaterialPreviousPosition (calm 0.4–1.7 px/frame, smooth); LOD r3 wired (culling, clipPosition, horizon closure). Distant flicker still 1.1–1.6× the reference without a LOD bias (look-dev item). 66/66 tests. Round 1 FAIL (close): open-water colours within 0–2 levels, but distant specular shimmer is 1.3–19× the reference (flickering dots on far crests); foam brightness not from SKY_LIGHT; view vector loses precision at 100 km. Round 2 starts when the refraction integration lands.

pieces.name: Refraction, shallow water, demo seabed via TERRAIN contracts
pieces.verdict: Builder: transparent-stage water reading scene.color/depth; open water bit-identical with refraction on/off; C6 diff vs reference 37→9 (golden). Refraction +0.7 ms under 4×MSAA. Reviewed in the integration wave.

pieces.name: Foam: persistent history + pattern
pieces.verdict: Review r1 FAIL (narrow, docs/port/reviews/foam-r1.md): robust (deterministic, frame-rate independent, origin-exact, 66/66 tests) but any history reset restarts foam from 0 (never recovers while paused); nothing declares it reads ocean.foam; asset hook not passed through createOceanGpu; dead fineInSource; foam debug views broken. Round 2: on-screen whitecap coverage within 1–6 % of the reference (was +15–30 %); history correlation 0.9996 with the reference; 0.03–0.08 ms GPU. Under review.

pieces.name: GPU readback parity (?parity) + floating test objects
pieces.verdict: GPU probe with 1-frame async readback, ?parity, ?buoy, tools/parity.mjs. GPU field vs CPU p99 < 1 % Hs on every tier and at 100 km; strict max < 2 % passes 8/32 (windy). Blockers: CPU heightAt inversion fails near steep crests (storm 0.6 m error); low tier drops c2 waves the CPU keeps; drawn surface is view-dependent (vertex mips beyond ~20 m, far fade from 200 m).

issues.text: Brightness comparisons: the WebGL reference page darkens its canvas with a CSS overlay (top 20 %, bottom 40 %) that is baked into the reference shots. With it applied to the port, the default view's luminance is 119.0 vs 119.6.
Core workers: a late snapshot job can corrupt heights by up to 7 m; a worker crash hangs the main thread.
Core: tick + gameplay queries p99 6.8–8.7 ms (target < 4 ms, workers off).
CPU heightAt inversion fails near steep crests (storm: 0.6 m error); parity max < 2 % Hs passes 8/32 cases.
Foam history reset restarts from zero and never recovers while paused; foam pass read not declared.
Decision needed: the drawn surface is view-dependent (vertex mips beyond ~20 m, far fade from 200 m); define the parity target.
README.md, TUNING.md (per-tier cost table) and HANDOFF.md not written yet.
Spec test command 'node --experimental-strip-types --test tests/' fails on Node 22.14 (directory argument); works with a glob. Engine targets Node 24.

log.text: Running passes finished. LOD r3, material r2 (precision, SKY_LIGHT foam, motion vectors) and the ?parity probe are built; core r2 and foam r1 reviews FAILED with clear next steps. Handoff for the next session written to docs/port/RESUME.md. Direction: working + spec-compliant first, look-dev in the engine.

Seabed refraction and foam now in the full ocean. Plan agreed direction: stop pixel-matching the WebGL tonemap (look-dev continues in the engine's HDR pipeline); fix correctness instead — material shimmer + 100 km precision + light-driven foam, foam coverage (+12 luminance over reference), core tick cost, ?parity readback. Then integration test and handoff docs.

Water material ported (all reference terms) and under review. Core and LOD failed round 1 and are being fixed (tick cost under gameplay load; horizon skirt tied to far plane). Refraction/seabed builder started. Shots below now use the new material; differences in 01/03/05 are mostly the missing seabed and foam history.
Core, LOD and GPU FFT built. FFT ocean renders on WebGPU at all four tiers. Critics reviewing core, LOD and FFT; material and foam builders started.
Read the spec, surveyed the WebGL reference, started infra, core and reference-analysis agents in parallel.
